description: Returns official records for a medicine from its brand or generic name (e.g. 'Advil', 'metformin'). For Canada: product identification, ingredients, status, company, schedule, route and form. For an EU or EEA country: the European Medicines Agency's authorisation, what it is approved for, shortages and safety letters. For the US (the default): whether it is over the counter or prescription, what the FDA label says it is for, its boxed warning and key warnings, a link to the full label (DailyMed), FDA recall reports, current FDA drug shortages, and what US pharmacies pay per tablet for each strength (CMS NADAC), brand next to generic. With `with` set to a second medicine, the result includes the label sentences where either label names the other; the absence of a mention is not evidence about safety. Applies to questions about what official records say about a medicine: its label, recalls, shortages or pharmacy cost. Not medical advice. Foods and medical devices are outside this result.

country.description: Country whose regulator is used: Canada uses Canadian product records; an EU or EEA country uses the European Medicines Agency; the US (the default) uses the FDA

name.description: Brand or generic name, e.g. 'Advil' or 'metformin'

with.description: Optional second medicine name; the result lists label sentences in either label that name the other

name: check_medicine
title: Medicine: FDA label, recalls, shortages, pharmacy cost
